4.2 Ablation Study
The attention-guided autoencoder module can be applied to feature representation with 
significant advantages of selective focus of diagnostically relevant areas at the sacrifice 
of background noise, which results in higher robustness and discriminative learning. The 
transformer-based global context modeling further enhances the performance to the 
extent that it captures long-range spatial associations and elaborate inter-feature 
associations that allow the model to interpret holistic patterns of lesions, as opposed to 
the local patterns only. Moreover, the hybrid hyperparameter optimization strategy is 
leading to efficiency and accuracy of the whole system because it systematically searches 
and optimizes the search space, guarantees the best choice of parameters, faster 
convergence, and enhanced generalization across a wide range of datasets. 
The ablation results on HAM10000 are discussed in Table 11 and indicate the 
performance enhancement of adding attention-based autoencoder, Transformer modules, 
and hybrid optimization. Each architectural and optimization component is proven to be

Comparative analysis was carried out of the non-optimized model with manually selected 
hyperparameters, models in which hyperparameters had been optimized individually 
using BO, GWO, and WOA, and the proposed hybrid-optimized model. The non-optimized 
model showed relatively poor performance since the parameter chosen was not optimal 
and was not adaptable enough. Although the individually optimized models showed some 
positive results in terms of accuracy and convergence due to the utilization of 
corresponding search mechanisms, they all had some limitations in the trade-offs 
between exploration and exploitation. On the contrary, the suggested hybrid-optimization 
model was the best of all as it was able to combine the advantages of BO, GWO, and WOA 
and thus achieve better generalization, high stability, and overall predictive performance.

4.5 Computational Efficiency and Complexity Analysis
The effectiveness of the proposed Attention-Guided Autoencoder with Transformer and 
Hybrid Bayesian GWO WOA optimization was measured in terms of training time, 
inference latency, parameter complexity, memory footprint, and scalability to clinical 
usage. Empirical research carried out using a multi-GPU setup (e.g., NVIDIA RTX/A100 
class GPU) suggests that even though the proposed hybrid architecture imposes some 
extra attention and transformer blocks on conventional CNNs, the optimized 
hyperparameter optimization will result in the stabilization of the convergence with fewer 
epochs, thus decreasing the training overhead. The average time per epoch of the training 
process was about 2.8 and 4.6 minutes on HAM10000 and ISIC-2019, respectively,

5 Discussion 
The proposed framework has demonstrated a high amount of quantitative performance 
regarding the HAM10000, ISIC-2019, and ISIC-2020 datasets, a high level of accuracy, 
and F1-score, and the value of the AUC, which demonstrates a high level of discriminative 
ability and a high level of reliability of melanoma detection with a small number of false 
negatives.
The qualitative analysis has determined that the model can be effective in focusing on the 
clinically significant features of lesions such as asymmetry, irregularity of borders, and 
changes in pigmentation and diminish the background noise and illumination artifact. 
Practically it has been determined that it has a low inference latency and can be trained 
to be cross-dataset stable which makes it applicable in real-time screening, tele-
dermatology, and decision-support systems. The challenges of integrating attention and 
transformer functionality can be simplified via optimized tokenization and optimized 
hyperparameter optimization enabling training with tolerable time and scalable 
inference, and deployment in circumstances where a GPU is used in clinical practice or 
on a server in the cloud. However, in practice, there are issues associated with 
implementation, including domain variations in imaging devices, regulatory acceptance 
terms, communication with hospital systems, and reliance on AI-based predictions in

legacy_cells.S: Classify dermoscopic lesion images as skin cancer/non-cancerous or into lesion classes.
legacy_cells.AJ: Attention-guided autoencoder encoder-decoder with lesion attention; transformer-inspired self-attention for global spatial context; classification head
legacy_cells.EK: Yes — architectural and optimizer-component ablations on HAM10000
legacy_cells.FL: Per-image pipeline: preprocessing/augmentation → attention-guided autoencoder embedding → transformer-inspired global-context module → classification head; hybrid Bayesian/GWO/WOA hyperparameter tuning during training.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes an attention-guided autoencoder plus transformer-inspired global-context skin-lesion classifier, with coordinated Bayesian, Grey Wolf, and Whale optimization for hyperparameter tuning.
legacy_cells.FN: Table 7 reports accuracy of 98.42% on HAM10000, 97.85% on ISIC-2019, and 98.67% on ISIC-2020.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors note reliance on mostly public dermoscopic datasets that may not represent clinical variability, need for multi-institutional clinical validation, computational complexity, and workflow integration/privacy concerns.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work: multimodal integration, edge-compatible model reduction, more explainability, and expanded clinical trials/validation.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports static image classification and dataset-level cross-dataset testing only; no temporal state transition, treatment/procedural action conditioning, patient-specific rollout, or planning/control is demonstrated.
